newsitem.title: UK: Natwest urges caution on MIRAS.
newsitem.headline: Natwest urges caution on MIRAS.

text.p: National Westminster Bank's mortgage lending arm said Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown should be careful not to dampen the housing market recovery by reducing tax relief on mortgage interest payments (MIRAS) in his July 2 budget.
NatWest Mortgage Services said it had conducted two surveys which showed property valuers thought abolishing MIRAS would make it more difficult for first-time buyers to take out a mortgage.
Thirty-four percent of existing mortgage holders said abolishing MIRAS would make it more difficult for them to meet their home loan payments.
There has been substantial press speculation that Brown might reduce or abolish mortgage interest relief in his first budget.

"The recovery in the housing market is still in its early stages and whilst no-one wants a return to the excesses of the 80s property boom, it is important that changes to MIRAS do not dampen the current market recovery," said George Wise, managing director of NatWest Mortgage Services.
Any changes would need to take account of the ability of borrowers to meet increased repayments, especially after recent rises in interest rates, he said.
